They are reference stand-ins pending replacement by stores produced on real hosts with the upstream command sequence below; until then no cross-host compatibility row (C1/C2/C7) may count them as upstream-origin evidence.

determinism.note: Randomness is exactly what upstream `secret init`/`set` draw from the libhydrogen PRNG, so a re-run reproduces identical decrypted contents and layout but not identical ciphertext bytes (plan §7.3 C6: ciphertext equality is NOT a compatibility requirement). The sha256 values pin the exact committed files.

upstream_commands.note: Exact commands the pinned upstream `secret` would run on a real host to produce an equivalent store (same names, values, physical order, ops_limit). Prompts are interactive on /dev/tty (never piped): at every `Passphrase: ` prompt enter P_A = "correct horse battery staple" in steps 2-7 and P_B = "second" in steps 8-10; steps 2 and 8 additionally prompt `No secrets stored with this passphrase.` + `Please, retype it to confirm: ` (new-partition confirmation) - re-enter the same passphrase. `update` with empty stdin keeps the old value while renaming in place, which is how the `DELETED:test` tombstone keeps its value `old\n` in the last P_A slot. Run with SECRET_AGENT unset.
